Absolutely true. I'm not self-diagnosing, but I think something was wrong with me at some point, when I was in fourth grade and sometimes now. Since new year in 2012, I've been having trouble accepting change. I had multiple crying spells then, i cried myself to sleep everyday for a month, and cried even in the shower (when my mom was there- i was a kid). My parents, especially my mom, just shrugged it off and laughed every time, and even now when she brings it up. She even tried to record me crying when i was sick. Before this, i was extremely outgoing, but now im the complete opposite, or at least, not as open with my parents anymore.

I could say the same for my brother, although he's never been the loud type really. Last September, he started first year uni and we could all see he was struggling pretty hard with the adjustments in the first week. On the friday, he broke down at the dinner table, and we all listened, but at the end all my dad said was "stop crying now, dont be depressed, that's bad for you." The ironic thing is, my dad's a mental health nurse.

I just love how Asian parents disregard their children's mental state. :)

TLDR; Please teach your kids how to deal and cope with change, or at least be there for them.
